evidence: test.sh is byte-identical to the frozen template test.sh (diff empty; task sha256 bd68259276ca...e5aa), so no task-specific launch assumption was added. Each launch assumption in task/tests/test.sh is stated to the agent: (1) entry file: test.sh:68 `[[ ! -f /app/server.js ]]` and :111 `node "$APP_ENTRY"` <- instruction.md:13 'It must start with node /app/server.js' and integration.md:5 'starts from /app/server.js'. (2) PORT: test.sh:108 `PORT="3000"`, probe on 127.0.0.1:3000 (:48) <- instruction.md:13 'listen on port 3000 (honour PORT if it's set)' and integration.md:5-6 'listens on port 3000 on 0.0.0.0' (covers the 127.0.0.1 probe vs a localhost/::1-only bind). (3) Liveness probe /api/health then / (test.sh:48) <- instruction.md:13 'expose GET /api/health as a check that never touches the database, serve the UI as well as the API from that one process'; integration.md:9-10. (4) DB_PATH: test.sh:98/101/109 sets DB_PATH=/app/app.db or /tmp/submission/app.db <- instruction.md:13 'keep its durable data in /app/app.db, honouring DB_PATH when that is set'; integration.md:7-8. (5) NODE_PATH/deps: test.sh:106 NODE_PATH=/usr/local/lib/node_modules under env -i <- instruction.md:13 'Server dependencies are already available, so don't install packages'; integration.md:3-4 'Express and better-sqlite3 already available through NODE_PATH; use only those packages and Node built-ins'; both images install express@5.1.0 and better-sqlite3@12.4.1 globally on node:22-bookworm-slim (environment/Dockerfile:3,9-11; tests/Dockerfile:1,9,16-21). (6) Symlink refusal (test.sh:72-83, zero reward for any link outside /app/node_modules or escaping it) <- task-added integration.md:16-19 states exactly this rule and forbids linking to the global install; this closes the template gap (template integration.md lacks these lines). (7) Seed: test.sh does not read seed; artifacts copy /app and /assets (task.toml:2); instruction.md:13-15 tells the agent to use /assets/seed_data.json and copy what it needs into /app since /assets is unavailable at runtime, which is conservative relative to the verifier (it actually supplies /assets and chmods it a+rX at test.sh:88), so no hidden dependency. (8) Fresh DB/restart persistence: restart helper relaunches with the same DB_PATH (test.sh:160-167) <- instruction.md:15 'keep new work across restarts'; integration.md:8-9. (9) Judge URL http://localhost:3000 (app_context.md:4) matches the stated port. (10) Sign-in accounts in app_context.md:8-19 match instruction.md:17 verbatim; per the workbook internal note and quality-checks.md ###23, a login surface is house convention, not a contract mismatch. No same-origin requirement appears anywhere (correct per public-network profile). Golden honors the contract cwd-independently: db.js:9-10 and index.js:42 resolve via __dirname, bootstrap.js:43 listens on PORT||3000 at 0.0.0.0, and workspace.cjs:16 shows the golden launched as `node /app/server.js` from cwd /tmp with only PATH/HOME/NODE_PATH/PORT/DB_PATH, matching test.sh's sanitized env (scripted run, uid 65534, hashes verified). Weak-app probe: a broken app whose /api/health returns 500 passes the test.sh probe (HTTPError counts as ready, test.sh:51-52) but that is a liveness-only gate by template design; the render/constraints judges are what exclude dead apps (rows 21/25 scope), not a contract disagreement. RISK REASONS (not a demonstrated defect): (a) Two launch conditions are implicit rather than stated: test.sh runs the app as uid 65534 (test.sh:110) and from the verifier's working directory, which per tests/Dockerfile:45 is /tests and is chmod go-rwx (test.sh:12, Dockerfile:44), whereas the agent image's WORKDIR is /app (environment/Dockerfile:25). A submission that resolves static files or its copied seed relative to process.cwd() (e.g. express.static('public'), fs.readFileSync('seed_data.json')) works when the agent tests it from /app but would serve nothing/crash under test.sh. The instruction's absolute entry command 'node /app/server.js' and 'Copy what you need into /app' reasonably imply cwd-independence, and the template test.sh is template-controlled, so I treat this as a latent P3 clarity point rather than a Fail. Non-root execution is harmless for the stated contract because test.sh chowns /app to 65534 (test.sh:87) or falls back to a writable copy. (b) No measured execution of this frozen test.sh against the frozen candidate exists in the raw-evidence index (its own scope: 'Full configured grading/workload ... absent'); the workspace.cjs run approximates but does not reproduce test.sh (cwd /tmp, not /tests; launched without setsid/setpriv wrapper in that line). Agreement is therefore established by source reading, not by a verifier launch log.
counterexample: Not a Fail. Latent conforming-alternative risk: an app built per the brief that uses express.static('public') or reads ./seed_data.json relative to cwd passes the agent's own checks from WORKDIR /app but, launched by test.sh from /tests as uid 65534, serves 404s/fails seeding and is zeroed at the render gate even though the brief never mentioned the launch cwd.
suggested_fix: Optional, task-side only (do not edit template test.sh): add one sentence to environment/instructions/integration.md such as 'The verifier launches node /app/server.js from an unrelated working directory as an unprivileged user, so resolve files relative to the server file, not the current directory.' Then obtain a real test.sh launch log on the frozen candidate for the runtime-evidence record.
